issues.legal_issue: A preliminary proclamation proposing to apply municipal legislation to an area is insufficient if it does not specify whether all or only some of the legislation’s purposes are proposed to be applied.
material_facts: The proclamation identified the villages proposed for inclusion and invited residents to submit objections.

It stated an intention to issue a notification under Section 417-A(1) but did not say whether administrative provision was proposed for all purposes of the Act or only some, or identify any selected purposes.
No objections were received, and a subsequent notification applied all provisions of the Act to the area.
issues.conclusion: The proclamation was ambiguous and incomplete, so the resulting notification was invalid; the High Court was justified in quashing it.
issues.legal_principle: Section 417-A(1) of the Orissa Municipal Act, 1950 permits administrative provision for all or any of the Act’s purposes in a notified area. Under Sections 417-A(1-a) and (1-b), residents must have an opportunity to object, and the State Government must consider objections and the District Magistrate’s views before issuing the notification. The preliminary proclamation must identify the proposed area and state whether all or only specified purposes are proposed, sufficiently clearly to enable residents to make informed objections. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.notified_area_proposal_challenge: The proceeding challenges a notification applying municipal legislation to an area as a notified area.
predicates.proclamation_invites_resident_objections: The government issued a preliminary proclamation inviting residents of the proposed area to object to its plan.
predicates.proclamation_omits_proposed_scope: The preliminary proclamation did not state whether the government proposed to apply all purposes or only specified purposes of the legislation.

issues.definition: When a challenge to a notified-area proposal concerns a proclamation that invites residents’ objections but omits the proposed scope, the resulting area notification is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: A preliminary proclamation published in a newspaper circulating in the proposed area must be in the local language residents understand, even though its publication in the Official Gazette may be in English.
material_facts: The proclamation was published in English in both the Official Gazette and a local newspaper circulating in the proposed area.
Oriya was the local language, and most residents did not know English.
Rule 602 did not prescribe the language for a proclamation under Section 417-A; the Oriya Gazette was published in English.
issues.conclusion: The proclamation should have been published in Oriya in the local newspaper; publication there in English did not meet the statutory purpose, and the resulting notification was invalid.
issues.legal_principle: Section 417-A(1-a) of the Orissa Municipal Act, 1950 requires publication of the proclamation in the Official Gazette and in at least one newspaper circulating in the area, so residents can understand the proposal and submit objections. The Gazette publication may be in English, but the newspaper publication must be in the local language familiar to residents. Rule 602 of the Orissa Municipal Rules, 1953 does not prescribe the language for this proclamation. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.notified_area_proposal_challenge: The proceeding challenges a notification applying municipal legislation to an area as a notified area.
predicates.proclamation_published_in_local_newspape: The government published the preliminary proclamation in a newspaper circulating in the proposed area.
predicates.newspaper_proclamation_not_in_residents_: The preliminary proclamation in that newspaper was not in the local language familiar to residents of the proposed area.

issues.definition: When a challenge to a notified-area proposal concerns a proclamation published in a local newspaper but not in the residents’ local language, the resulting area notification is invalid.
